hints: Focus on which functional group can actually be broken apart by dilute acid, an ester link or an alcohol group?
Write out the acid hydrolysis for each ester as carboxylic acid plus alcohol, for example the first ester gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ plus a diol fragment.
Simplify each pair of molecular formulas down to the simplest whole number ratio and look for the pair that both reduce to the same ratio.
walkthrough:
**Spot what can be hydrolysed**

Only esters are hydrolysed by dilute $\text{HCl(aq)}$ to give a carboxylic acid and an alcohol.

General acid hydrolysis:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Eliminate the non-ester**

Option D, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a diol with only $\text{C-OH}$ groups. It has no ester link, so it cannot be hydrolysed. We only test A, B and C.

**Write the hydrolysis products for B**

Q in B is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, an ester made from ethanoic acid and a hydroxy-acid.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$$
So products are ethanoic acid, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$, and 3-hydroxypropanoic acid, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3$.

**Compare empirical formulas**

Simplify each molecular formula by dividing by the common factor.
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{O}$$
Both reduce to the same empirical formula, so this fits the question perfectly.

options.A: Hydrolysis gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$) and $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$). Their empirical formulas are $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{O}$, which are different.
options.B: Hydrolysis gives ethanoic acid $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$ and $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3$. Both simplify to the empirical formula $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$, so the condition is met.
options.C: This is propyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Hydrolysis gives propanoic acid $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ and propan-1-ol $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$. Their empirical formulas $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ and $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$ are different.
options.D: This is hexane-3,4-diol, an alcohol not an ester. Alcohols do not undergo hydrolysis with $\text{HCl(aq)}$, so no hydrolysis products are formed at all.
